input.issue_gist: LocalDate.fromCalendarFields (and likely LocalDateTime.fromCalendarFields) ignores Calendar.ERA, so a BC-era GregorianCalendar date is treated as an AD year instead of being converted to the proper Joda year (e.g. year 0 or negative).

concrete_examples.input: GregorianCalendar cal = new GregorianCalendar(1, Calendar.JANUARY, 3); cal.set(Calendar.ERA, GregorianCalendar.BC); LocalDate.fromCalendarFields(cal);
concrete_examples.expected: LocalDate of year 0 (1 BC = ISO year 0): 0000-01-03
concrete_examples.actual: LocalDate of year 1 (AD): 0001-01-03, because ERA is ignored

concrete_examples.input: GregorianCalendar cal with year 2 and ERA = BC, month Jan, day 3; LocalDate.fromCalendarFields(cal);

content.text:
The failures reproduce the reported bug, and none of the concerns in (4), (5) or (6) applies.

- **Inputs match the conditions.** The test builds a `GregorianCalendar` with year `yearOfEra`, sets `ERA = BC`, and calls `LocalDate.fromCalendarFields`. The logged outputs are `0165-12-03` for year 165 and `0020-07-20` for year 20. Both are the AD years, so the era was ignored. The correct results are year `1 - 165 = -164` and `1 - 20 = -19`.
- **The error matches the expected behavior.** The assertion failure `expected:<-1786> but was:<1787>` has the same pattern. The expected value is the BC-converted Joda year, and the actual value is the plain `Calendar.YEAR`. The source confirms the cause: `fromCalendarFields` reads only `calendar.get(Calendar.YEAR)` and never checks `Calendar.ERA`.
- **Same root cause.** Month and day are correct, and no exception is thrown. Only the year is wrong, and it is wrong because the era is ignored.
- **(4) `buggyIf` is not too wide.** `buggyIf = bc` means the calendar is always set to BC. Every BC date with year of era ≥ 1 is converted incorrectly, so the buggy code is never already correct on an input the test accepts. The expected value `1 - yearOfEra` is the right ISO year for BC dates.
- **(5) `buggyIf` is not too narrow.** Only BC-era calendars trigger the bug. AD dates are already handled correctly.
- **(6) The valid domain is adequately covered.** Years run 1–2000, months 1–12 and days 1–28. These are all legal calendar values, and they are not restricted to the bug-triggering inputs.

The failing inputs are printed as `(…, 0)` for the boolean, which looks like `bc = false`. If `bc` were false, `assumeTrue(buggyIf)` would have rejected the input before the call. The logged results show the calendar was set to BC, so the `0` is probably just how the boolean is printed. The quoted stack trace values (-1786 and 1787) also don't match the two listed inputs. They most likely come from a different failing input of the same kind.
